column10: This position is a 100% teaching appointment. Instructional duties will include teaching in our first-year introductory biology sequence, with advising. 1) Not on the search committee, but in the department and happy to answer questions. One thing to note is that UMaine's lectuers are unionized and go up for tenure equivalent (including earned sabbaticals). 2) Salary Range? +1 3) curious if there are opportunities for lecturers to participate in research activites/resources etc, even though it isn't TT 4) @2 UMaine's salaries are public, so I would recommend looking up the range. Because this is a MS or PhD position, salary will vary; the last person who had the position was paid $62,000/year after reaching Senior Lecturuer/just cause status. @3 there are lecturers who participate in research but this is not part of their duties and would not be included in their review except as ancillary information. This is basicaly to prevent the unviersity from hiring "cheaper" TT faculty, as lecturers are 100% teaching positions, with a higher teaching load. However, it's not uncommon for lecturers to participate in pedagogy research, and we even have 1-2 lectuers in our college who have had graudate students and who do participate in non-pedagogy research. As a 10.5-month position you would still be eligible to add 1.5 months of summer salary, and could be a member of the graduate faculty, and are able to participate in all the same professional development trainings, apply for internal grants, etc. 5) @1 could you elaborate on your comment "lecturers are unionized and go up for tenure equivalent"? What is the tenure-equivalent of non-TS? @ 5 There is no tenure equivalent.  You either get it or you don't.  The mumbo jumbo handed out otherwise is bait and switch.  Such positions are secure until they are not.  Been there, am there, would do it again.  Its just like anything else.  These are jobs, if you need a job, its better than unemployed.  ;)  6) @5 another department member here; this position would get a continuing contract after 5 years at which point you can only be fired for just cause or retrenchment (layoffs for financial emergencies or programatic reasons) , which is the same as what professors get and which is protected by the same union. 7) OP/1 here again; there is a formal process of tenure-equivalence for lecturers, as 6 notes. Lecturers are evaluated every year along with TT faculty, they go up for and are promoted to "senior lectuer" after achiving just-cause status (and announced along with the TT promotions to Associate), they get sabbaticals after just cause and every 6 years just like TT faculty. We have multiple people in our unit who have done this (one even served as department chair as lecturer) and my spouse is going up for just cause this fall in another department. It's not a "bait and switch mumbo jumbo" phrase, it has real, legal meaning and a union contract.

column10: Dept is looking for an evolutionary ecologist who can connect with a theme of "adaptation and resilience." Department is strong in molecular approaches and ad invokes both ecology and evolution. Job does not specify any particular focal organisms(s) but Iowa campus has a restored prarie site, is close to other similar sites and native/restored oak-hickory forests.Teaching (1 course/semester + graduate student mentoring) is emphasized. Iowa City looks like a great place to live. 1) Amazing position :D 2) Iowa City is a great place to live: bicycling, curbside compost, farmer's market, progressive city/county councils (listen to Rock Hard Causcus), fast snow removal from streets and quick clean up from tornados/storms, many people with small prarie gardens, and free buses but depending on where you live biking and driving might be better, there are multiple festivals in the summer when its nice and quiet but no big names, and many cute cafes/boutiques. My dislikes were so many drunk students downtown like - vomit on the streets some nights, persumably conservatives the city come into the city to intimidate progressive students (Iowa politics in general suck), not enough restuarants and unfortnately many are getting their ingredients from Sysco. When it comes to the biology department almost all labs focus on genetics in some way, if you are an Evolutionary Ecologist that loves genetics this would be a great department for you. Now, if you are more of a Quantitative or Field Ecologist you might have a more difficult time getting hired because the hiring committee likes to see experiments that use DNA sequencing, gene knock-down, transcriptomics, etc. I was a graduate student there so take what I say about the position with a grain of salt. @ 0) The prarie is recently established (~5 years) and it about an acre of land, they did start another native plant prarie right next to 2 years ago, but the prarie is right in the center of the cross country track field so if you need to be mindful of track events going on (track is mroe important than your science).
